paragraphs: This page introduces the five-part BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook Agricultural Workers combined group: crop and nursery greenhouse farmworkers 45-2092, farm, ranch and aquacultural animal farmworkers 45-2093, agricultural equipment operators 45-2091, animal breeders 45-2021 and other agricultural workers 45-2099. The first three are the focus directions compared on this page, not the whole group. The Handbook marks the combined SOC with a dash in its projection table; 45-2090 is a different four-part group that excludes animal breeders, so the combined group's 831,900 positions and 35,890 U.S. dollars must not be pasted onto 45-2090. First check the work objects, the specific duties, the seasonal hours and the safety conditions, and then decide whether you are willing to do on-site work in the long term.

Three paper self-test tasks are given in AW27-V1: calculate the acceptable net weight and the amount set aside from a simulated harvest weight; check a simulated pen feeding shortfall and the anomaly; and decide from a simulated machinery-guard record whether to pause. Use only the task material and pen and paper or a spreadsheet, with no contact with animals, pesticides or running machinery. It demonstrates calculation, recording and escalation methods and cannot prove physical tolerance or a real operating qualification. (Editorial exercise.)

People who are more likely to adapt: those who can sustain physical work outdoors in all weather, work with others to the crew's arrangements, are willing to operate machinery to the procedures and report anomalies honestly, and do not mind seasonal overtime and repetitive movement. If heat and cold, dust and animal contact are hard to accept, or you are unwilling to wear protective equipment to the safety procedures, the risk is usually greater.

Insufficient evidence: no Chinese wage or recruitment education sample for this occupation was obtained; U.S. material cannot be used to infer a Chinese qualification. The U.S. headline figures use the five-part Handbook combined group: a median annual wage of 35,890 U.S. dollars in 2025, month 5 (May), 831,900 positions in 2025, about −2% over 2025—2035 and 111,500 openings per year on average; the combined group is not 45-2090. The main text lists the same-period detail projections for the three focus directions separately, so the group's percentiles cannot be averaged or applied directly. The Chinese National Bureau of Statistics provides only industry and unit-type background.

In one sentence: a set of positions that carry out planting, care, harvesting, feeding and machinery work in fields, greenhouses, ranches or farms; the emphasis is completing the work safely and recording it honestly, and with training and authorisation a worker may also take part in routine adjustments, work organisation or sales, while overall responsibility for running the farm business belongs to management positions.

The on-site work of agricultural workers includes crop planting and harvesting, nursery and greenhouse care, livestock, poultry and aquaculture feeding, and machinery operation. 45-2092, 45-2093 and 45-2091 focus on crops, animals and equipment respectively; the BLS Handbook also covers animal breeders 45-2021 and other agricultural workers 45-2099. The breeding direction involves selecting animals to mate and keeping breeding and offspring-characteristic records, so the whole group must not be described as doing only the three kinds of physical work.

The five-part Handbook combined group had 831,900 positions in 2025; the parts are crops 546,800, animals 202,100, equipment 66,900, other 9,300 and breeding 6,900, and the official note says the parts may not add exactly because of rounding. The four-part group 45-2090 had 825,000 positions with a median wage of 35,870 U.S. dollars, which differs from this page's combined group. The specific O*NET SOC pages give the corresponding detail tasks and no single group-wide profile.

Outdoor conditions｜65% work outdoors in all weather every day, and 40% are exposed to extreme heat or cold every day (45-2092 respondent shares); 45-2093 report 65% outdoors every day and 44% exposure to extreme heat or cold once a month or more often but less than weekly.
Physical demands and posture｜57% use their hands on tools and objects continuously or almost continuously, 51% make repetitive movements continuously or almost continuously and 49% bend or twist continuously or almost continuously (45-2092).
Working hours｜56% work more than 40 hours per week (45-2092), and overtime is marked during the busy and harvest seasons.
Exposure and protection｜In 45-2093, 61% are exposed to contaminants every day and 48% are exposed to minor burns, cuts, bites or stings every day; in 45-2092, 29% wear routine protective equipment every day and 29% are exposed to contaminants every day.
Safety responsibility｜In 45-2092, 38% have a high level of responsibility for the health and safety of others; machinery and animal work requires following the safety procedures.
Decision freedom｜In 45-2092, 29% have a great deal of freedom in deciding tasks and priorities and 24% a great deal of freedom in decision-making, while the work is mostly carried out to arrangements.
Communication and collaboration｜In 45-2092, 74% have face-to-face or personal and team discussions every day and 39% consider cooperation with a team important.
Time pressure｜In 45-2092, 49% face time pressure every day, concentrated especially at points such as harvest and moving groups.
Noise and temperature｜In 45-2093, 52% are exposed to distracting noise once a month or more often but less than weekly.

This page focuses on the three directions of crops and nursery greenhouse, animal feeding and machinery operation; the BLS combined group also includes breeding and other agricultural workers, so the three directions are not the whole.

The five-part Handbook combined group has a median annual wage of 35,890 U.S. dollars and an hourly wage of 17.25 U.S. dollars in 2025, month 5 (May); it is projected to decline by about 2% over 2025—2035, and the 111,500 openings per year come from replacement demand. Most positions need no formal education credential, but animal breeders typically require high school; equipment operation training may be longer. The BLS same-period details are equipment +8.6%, crops −2.4%, animals −3.2%, other +3.8% and breeding +3.0%; the combined group and the details are used separately and no other statistical period is spliced on.

Before starting, check at least six things: the detail direction (crop and nursery greenhouse／animal feeding／machinery operation); the employer type (farm／ranch and livestock farm／agricultural enterprise or cooperative); the pay basis (hourly／piece rate／seasonal lump sum); the operating permits (driving and farm-machinery operation, pesticide use); the accommodation, transport and labour-protection arrangements; and the working hours, seasonality and overtime arrangements.

Development and stability: whether skills training is provided, whether a move into machinery operation or a technical support position is possible, and the off-season arrangements.

O*NET 45-2092 shows that 65% of respondents work outdoors in all weather every day, 57% use their hands continuously, 51% make repetitive movements continuously, 49% bend or twist continuously and 56% work more than 40 hours per week.

entries.answer: The three directions are only focus examples, and the BLS group also contains breeding and other agricultural workers.
